# Invite email, CSV export, and seven-day expiration

Label: needs-triage

## Problem Statement

Creating an invite currently only stores the guest's name, email address, phone number, and creation time in memory. The guest is not notified, invite operators cannot export the invite list, and an invite has no defined lifetime. This leaves guests unaware of their invitation and operators without a portable record or a reliable way to distinguish usable invites from stale ones.

## Solution

Extend invite management so that creating an `Invite` sends an email to the invite's email address, every invite expires exactly seven days after its creation time, and operators can export all invite records and their lifecycle data as CSV. Keep these behaviors behind `InviteService`, use the existing `Notifier` abstraction for delivery, and make time-dependent behavior deterministic through the service's injected clock.

## User Stories

1. As a guest, I want to receive an email when my invite is created, so that I know I have been invited.
2. As a guest, I want the invite email sent to the email address on my invite, so that the notification reaches the intended recipient.
3. As a guest, I want the invite email to identify itself as an invitation, so that I understand why I received it.
4. As an invite operator, I want invite creation to retain the guest's name, email address, phone number, and creation time, so that existing invite records remain complete.
5. As an invite operator, I want each invite to have an expiration time seven days after creation, so that its validity window is explicit.
6. As an invite operator, I want an invite to remain active before its expiration time, so that it can be used throughout the seven-day window.
7. As an invite operator, I want an invite to be expired at its expiration time and afterward, so that validity has an unambiguous boundary.
8. As an invite operator, I want expiration status evaluated against the current time, so that the status remains accurate without manually updating stored records.
9. As an invite operator, I want to export every invite, including active and expired invites, so that the export is a complete historical snapshot.
10. As an invite operator, I want the CSV to contain the invite's name, email address, phone number, creation time, expiration time, and current expiration status, so that all invite and lifecycle data is portable.
11. As an invite operator, I want a header row in the CSV, so that each column is identifiable.
12. As an invite operator, I want one data row per invite, so that records can be processed by spreadsheet and data tools.
13. As an invite operator, I want CSV values to be escaped according to the CSV format, so that commas, quotes, and line breaks in invite data do not corrupt the export.
14. As an invite operator, I want date-time values represented consistently, so that exported creation and expiration times can be compared and parsed.
15. As an invite operator, I want an export with no invites to still contain its headers, so that downstream tools receive a valid, self-describing CSV.
16. As a developer, I want notification delivery to use the existing `Notifier` interface, so that production transports and recorded test notifications remain interchangeable.
17. As a developer, I want expiration calculations to use the injected clock, so that boundary behavior can be tested deterministically.
18. As a developer, I want CSV generation separated from notification transport, so that exports do not send notifications or otherwise mutate invites.
19. As a developer, I want exporting invite data to be read-only, so that repeated exports do not change invite state.
20. As a developer, I want existing callers of invite creation to continue receiving the created `Invite`, so that the current service contract remains compatible.

## Implementation Decisions

- Extend the `Invite` domain model with lifecycle behavior derived from `created_at`: `expires_at` is exactly seven days later, and an invite is expired when the comparison time is greater than or equal to `expires_at`.
- Keep `InviteService` as the public orchestration boundary for creation, notification, lifecycle evaluation, and exporting the service's invite collection.
- On successful creation, send one email through `Notifier.send_email` to the new invite's email address. Do not send an SMS; the existing phone field remains invite data only.
- Preserve the existing creation return value and stored invite fields.
- Introduce a focused CSV serialization module or equivalent deep module with a small interface that accepts invite records plus a comparison time and returns standards-compliant CSV text. It owns column order, escaping, date-time serialization, header-only empty output, and derived lifecycle columns.
- Export records in their stored order to make output stable and predictable.
- The CSV columns are `name`, `email`, `phone`, `created_at`, `expires_at`, and `status`; `status` is `active` or `expired` at export time.
- Serialize date-times in ISO 8601 form, preserving the semantics of the existing clock values rather than silently changing time zones.
- Include all invites in the export regardless of lifecycle status. Expiration changes validity, not retention.
- CSV export is side-effect free: it does not send notifications, remove expired invites, or modify stored records.
- No HTTP, persistence, or user-interface layer currently exists in the project; this work exposes the behavior through the invite domain/service interfaces rather than inventing such a layer.
- Delivery-failure semantics are not established by the current codebase. Triage must decide whether a notifier exception should leave the newly stored invite in place or make creation atomic before implementation begins.
- The exact customer-facing email subject and body are not established in the current product vocabulary. Triage must provide or approve that copy; tests should assert the approved contract without coupling to transport internals.

## Testing Decisions

- Tests should verify externally observable behavior through `InviteService`, returned `Invite` values, recorded notifications, and exported CSV content. They should not assert private helper calls or internal implementation structure.
- Extend the existing `unittest` suite and follow its prior art: inject a fixed clock into `InviteService` and use `RecordingNotifier` to observe messages without a real transport.
- Test invite creation stores and returns the invite while recording exactly one email to the invite's email address with the approved subject and body.
- Test that creation does not send an SMS.
- Test `expires_at` is exactly seven days after `created_at`.
- Test lifecycle behavior immediately before expiration, exactly at expiration, and after expiration using controlled date-times.
- Test CSV output for zero, one, and multiple invites, including stable headers and stored ordering.
- Test that the CSV includes active and expired invites and derives each status using a single controlled export time.
- Test CSV escaping with commas, quotes, and line breaks in supported text fields by parsing the output with a standards-compliant CSV reader.
- Test ISO 8601 serialization for creation and expiration values.
- Test repeated exports return equivalent output for the same invite collection and comparison time and do not mutate invites or record notifications.
- Once delivery-failure semantics are resolved in triage, add a service-level test that makes `Notifier.send_email` raise and verifies the agreed storage and exception behavior.

## Out of Scope

- SMS notifications.
- Reminder or expiration-notification emails.
- Resending, revoking, deleting, accepting, or redeeming invites.
- Automatically deleting expired invite records.
- Importing CSV data.
- Filtering or selecting a subset of invites for export.
- Adding database persistence, an HTTP API, authentication, authorization, or a graphical interface.
- Choosing or configuring a production email provider.
- Changing guest display-name formatting or pricing behavior.

## Further Notes

- The current service stores invites in memory, and this PRD preserves that architecture.
- The seven-day lifetime is a duration from each invite's recorded creation time, not seven calendar dates.
- “All invite data” is interpreted as the existing invite fields plus the lifecycle values required by this feature. The explicit CSV schema above prevents accidental omission or unstable column ordering.
- This issue intentionally carries `needs-triage` because notification failure semantics and final email copy require product or engineering confirmation before execution.

# Invite SMS, seven-day expiration, and Arabic display names

Label: needs-triage

## Problem Statement

Creating an invite currently stores the guest's details but does not notify the guest or define how long the invite remains valid. In addition, the guest-list display-name formatter converts truncated names through ASCII decoding, which removes Arabic characters and can leave Arabic guest names blank. Legal requires invite notifications to use SMS only: invite emails must not be sent, and the previously proposed CSV export is cancelled.

## Solution

When an `Invite` is created, send one SMS to its phone number through the existing `Notifier`, never send an invite email, and make the invite expire exactly seven days after creation. Update guest display-name formatting to preserve Arabic and other Unicode text while retaining its existing whitespace cleanup, title formatting, and length-limiting purpose. Do not add CSV export behavior.

## User Stories

1. As a guest, I want to receive an SMS when my invite is created, so that I know I have been invited.
2. As a guest, I want the invite SMS sent to the phone number recorded on my invite, so that it reaches the intended recipient.
3. As a guest, I want the SMS to identify itself as an invitation, so that I understand why I received it.
4. As a guest, I do not want an invite email sent, so that notifications comply with the SMS-only legal requirement.
5. As an invite operator, I want exactly one SMS sent for each successfully created invite, so that guests are notified once without duplicate messages.
6. As an invite operator, I want invite creation to retain the guest's name, email address, phone number, and creation time, so that the existing invite record remains complete even though email is not a notification channel.
7. As an invite operator, I want each invite to have an expiration time seven days after creation, so that its validity window is explicit.
8. As an invite operator, I want an invite to remain active before its expiration time, so that it can be used throughout the seven-day window.
9. As an invite operator, I want an invite to be expired at its expiration time and afterward, so that the validity boundary is unambiguous.
10. As an invite operator, I want expiration evaluated against the current time, so that invite status remains accurate without manually changing stored records.
11. As an invite operator, I want expired invites retained in the invite collection, so that expiration does not silently delete guest records.
12. As an Arabic-speaking guest, I want my Arabic name preserved in the guest list, so that my identity is visible rather than displayed as blank.
13. As a guest whose name uses non-ASCII characters, I want my name preserved during display formatting, so that valid Unicode names are not discarded.
14. As an invite operator, I want leading and trailing whitespace removed from display names, so that the guest list remains tidy.
15. As an invite operator, I want long display names safely shortened without corrupting Unicode characters, so that the guest list remains readable.
16. As an invite operator, I want existing Latin-name title formatting to continue working, so that the current guest-list presentation does not regress.
17. As a developer, I want SMS delivery to use the existing `Notifier` interface, so that production transports and recorded test notifications remain interchangeable.
18. As a developer, I want expiration calculations to use the injected clock, so that boundary behavior can be tested deterministically.
19. As a developer, I want display-name formatting to remain a focused, independently testable function, so that multilingual behavior can be verified without invite-service setup.
20. As a developer, I want existing callers of invite creation to continue receiving the created `Invite`, so that the current service contract remains compatible.
21. As a legal stakeholder, I want the invite workflow to make no call to the email notification method, so that future refactoring does not accidentally reintroduce invite emails.
22. As a product stakeholder, I do not want CSV export added, so that the cancelled capability does not appear in the service contract.

## Implementation Decisions

- Keep `InviteService` as the public orchestration boundary for creating, storing, notifying, and evaluating invites.
- On successful creation, send exactly one SMS through `Notifier.send_sms` to the new invite's phone number.
- Do not call `Notifier.send_email` during invite creation. The email address remains part of the existing `Invite` record but is not used for notification.
- Preserve the existing creation return value and stored invite fields.
- Extend the `Invite` domain model with lifecycle behavior derived from `created_at`: `expires_at` is exactly seven days later, and an invite is expired when the comparison time is greater than or equal to `expires_at`.
- Evaluate expiration from recorded times rather than scheduling mutation or deletion. Expiration changes validity, not retention.
- Continue using the service's injected clock for creation and current-time comparisons.
- Keep display-name formatting as a small, deep module that accepts a guest name and length limit and returns presentation text.
- Make display-name truncation Unicode-safe. Apply the configured limit to characters rather than encoded bytes so truncation cannot split a multibyte character, and do not convert the result through ASCII.
- Preserve leading/trailing whitespace removal and the existing Latin title-casing behavior. Valid Arabic text must remain visible; casing rules that do not apply to Arabic must not remove or replace it.
- Do not introduce CSV serialization, export methods, export schemas, or download behavior.
- No HTTP, persistence, or user-interface layer currently exists in the project; expose lifecycle behavior through the invite domain/service interfaces and correct the existing display formatter rather than inventing new layers.
- Notification delivery-failure semantics are not established by the current codebase. Triage must decide whether an SMS transport exception leaves the stored invite in place or makes creation atomic before implementation begins.
- The exact customer-facing SMS body is not established in the current product vocabulary. Triage must provide or approve that copy; tests should assert the approved contract without coupling to transport internals.

## Testing Decisions

- Tests should verify externally observable behavior through `InviteService`, returned `Invite` values, `RecordingNotifier.sent`, lifecycle results, and `display_name` output. They should not assert private helper calls or internal implementation structure.
- Extend the existing `unittest` suite and follow its prior art: inject a fixed clock into `InviteService`, use `RecordingNotifier` instead of a real transport, and test `display_name` directly.
- Test that invite creation stores and returns the invite while recording exactly one SMS to the invite's phone number with the approved body.
- Test explicitly that invite creation records no email notification.
- Test multiple invite creations produce one SMS per invite without duplicates or cross-addressing phone numbers.
- Test that `expires_at` is exactly seven days after `created_at`.
- Test lifecycle behavior immediately before expiration, exactly at expiration, and after expiration using controlled date-times.
- Test that evaluating expiration does not remove or mutate the stored invite.
- Add a regression test proving a wholly Arabic guest name produces a non-blank display name and preserves its text.
- Test Arabic names at, below, and above the length limit to prove truncation is Unicode-safe and deterministic.
- Test mixed Arabic and Latin names, as well as representative non-ASCII names, to guard against another ASCII-only implementation.
- Preserve the existing Latin-name title-casing test and add coverage for leading and trailing whitespace.
- Test that the formatter never returns blank solely because a non-blank input contains Arabic characters.
- Do not add CSV tests; the capability is cancelled and absent from the product contract.
- Once delivery-failure semantics are resolved in triage, add a service-level test that makes `Notifier.send_sms` raise and verifies the agreed storage and exception behavior.

## Out of Scope

- Invite email notifications of any kind.
- CSV export, CSV import, or downloadable invite reports.
- Notification channels other than SMS.
- Reminder or expiration-notification messages.
- Resending, revoking, deleting, accepting, or redeeming invites.
- Automatically deleting expired invite records.
- Adding database persistence, an HTTP API, authentication, authorization, or a graphical interface.
- Choosing or configuring a production SMS provider.
- Translating or localizing the SMS body.
- Changing pricing behavior.

## Further Notes

- This PRD supersedes the earlier email-and-CSV proposal. Email is prohibited for invite creation, and CSV work is cancelled.
- The current service stores invites in memory, and this PRD preserves that architecture.
- The seven-day lifetime is a duration from each invite's recorded creation time, not seven calendar dates.
- The Arabic-name issue is an existing display defect: byte truncation followed by ASCII decoding drops Arabic characters. Unicode-safe character truncation addresses the cause while retaining the formatter's role.
- This issue carries `needs-triage` because SMS delivery-failure semantics and final SMS copy still require product or engineering confirmation before execution.

# Invite SMS, 30-day expiration, finance CSV, and Arabic display names

Label: needs-triage

## Problem Statement

Creating an invite currently stores the guest's details but does not notify the guest or define how long the invite remains valid. Finance also lacks a portable invite list containing the guest details it needs. In addition, the guest-list display-name formatter converts truncated names through ASCII decoding, which removes Arabic characters and can leave Arabic guest names blank. Legal requires invite notifications to use SMS only, and finance requires a narrowly scoped CSV containing only guest name and phone number. Invites must expire after 30 days.

## Solution

When an `Invite` is created, send one SMS to its phone number through the existing `Notifier`, never send an invite email, and make the invite expire exactly 30 days after creation. Give finance a CSV export of all invites with exactly two columns, `name` and `phone`, and no other invite data. Update guest display-name formatting to preserve Arabic and other Unicode text while retaining its existing whitespace cleanup, title formatting, and length-limiting purpose.

## User Stories

1. As a guest, I want to receive an SMS when my invite is created, so that I know I have been invited.
2. As a guest, I want the invite SMS sent to the phone number recorded on my invite, so that it reaches the intended recipient.
3. As a guest, I want the SMS to identify itself as an invitation, so that I understand why I received it.
4. As a guest, I do not want an invite email sent, so that notifications comply with the SMS-only legal requirement.
5. As an invite operator, I want exactly one SMS sent for each successfully created invite, so that guests are notified once without duplicate messages.
6. As an invite operator, I want invite creation to retain the guest's name, email address, phone number, and creation time, so that the existing invite record remains complete even though email is not a notification channel or finance export field.
7. As an invite operator, I want each invite to have an expiration time 30 days after creation, so that its validity window is explicit.
8. As an invite operator, I want an invite to remain active before its expiration time, so that it can be used throughout the 30-day window.
9. As an invite operator, I want an invite to be expired at its expiration time and afterward, so that the validity boundary is unambiguous.
10. As an invite operator, I want expiration evaluated against the current time, so that invite status remains accurate without manually changing stored records.
11. As an invite operator, I want expired invites retained in the invite collection, so that expiration does not silently delete guest records.
12. As a finance user, I want to export all invites as CSV, so that I can use the invite list in finance workflows.
13. As a finance user, I want the CSV to contain each guest's recorded name and phone number, so that I receive the two fields needed for my work.
14. As a privacy stakeholder, I want the finance CSV limited to exactly name and phone, so that email addresses, timestamps, expiration data, status, and other invite data are not disclosed.
15. As a finance user, I want a header row containing `name` and `phone`, so that the two columns are identifiable.
16. As a finance user, I want one data row per invite, including active and expired invites, so that the export is a complete invite list.
17. As a finance user, I want export rows in the same order as the stored invites, so that repeated exports are predictable.
18. As a finance user, I want names and phone numbers escaped according to the CSV format, so that commas, quotes, and line breaks do not corrupt the export.
19. As a finance user, I want an empty invite list to produce a header-only CSV, so that the output remains valid and self-describing.
20. As an Arabic-speaking guest, I want my Arabic name preserved in the guest list, so that my identity is visible rather than displayed as blank.
21. As a guest whose name uses non-ASCII characters, I want my name preserved during display formatting, so that valid Unicode names are not discarded.
22. As an invite operator, I want leading and trailing whitespace removed from display names, so that the guest list remains tidy.
23. As an invite operator, I want long display names safely shortened without corrupting Unicode characters, so that the guest list remains readable.
24. As an invite operator, I want existing Latin-name title formatting to continue working, so that the current guest-list presentation does not regress.
25. As a developer, I want SMS delivery to use the existing `Notifier` interface, so that production transports and recorded test notifications remain interchangeable.
26. As a developer, I want expiration calculations to use the injected clock, so that boundary behavior can be tested deterministically.
27. As a developer, I want finance CSV serialization isolated behind a small interface, so that its strict field allowlist and CSV behavior can be tested independently.
28. As a developer, I want CSV export to be read-only, so that exporting does not notify guests or mutate invite records.
29. As a developer, I want display-name formatting to remain a focused, independently testable function, so that multilingual behavior can be verified without invite-service setup.
30. As a developer, I want existing callers of invite creation to continue receiving the created `Invite`, so that the current service contract remains compatible.
31. As a legal stakeholder, I want the invite workflow to make no call to the email notification method, so that future refactoring does not accidentally reintroduce invite emails.

## Implementation Decisions

- Keep `InviteService` as the public orchestration boundary for creating, storing, notifying, evaluating, and exporting invites.
- On successful creation, send exactly one SMS through `Notifier.send_sms` to the new invite's phone number.
- Do not call `Notifier.send_email` during invite creation. The email address remains part of the existing `Invite` record but is not used for notification.
- Preserve the existing creation return value and stored invite fields.
- Extend the `Invite` domain model with lifecycle behavior derived from `created_at`: `expires_at` is exactly 30 days later, and an invite is expired when the comparison time is greater than or equal to `expires_at`.
- Evaluate expiration from recorded times rather than scheduling mutation or deletion. Expiration changes validity, not retention.
- Continue using the service's injected clock for creation and current-time comparisons.
- Introduce a focused finance CSV serializer, or equivalent deep module, that accepts invite records and returns standards-compliant CSV text.
- The finance CSV schema is an explicit allowlist with exactly two columns in this order: `name`, `phone`. It must not include email, creation time, expiration time, lifecycle status, or any additional current or future invite field.
- Export the recorded invite name rather than the shortened guest-list display name, so finance does not receive presentation-truncated data.
- Include all stored invites, both active and expired, in stored order. Expiration changes validity but does not remove a record from the finance list.
- Produce a header-only document for an empty collection and use standard CSV quoting and escaping for every row.
- Make finance export side-effect free: it does not send notifications, evaluate away records, remove expired invites, or modify stored data.
- Keep display-name formatting as a small, deep module that accepts a guest name and length limit and returns presentation text.
- Make display-name truncation Unicode-safe. Apply the configured limit to characters rather than encoded bytes so truncation cannot split a multibyte character, and do not convert the result through ASCII.
- Preserve leading/trailing whitespace removal and the existing Latin title-casing behavior. Valid Arabic text must remain visible; casing rules that do not apply to Arabic must not remove or replace it.
- No HTTP, persistence, or graphical interface currently exists in the project; expose these behaviors through domain/service interfaces rather than inventing new layers.
- Notification delivery-failure semantics are not established by the current codebase. Triage must decide whether an SMS transport exception leaves the stored invite in place or makes creation atomic before implementation begins.
- The exact customer-facing SMS body is not established in the current product vocabulary. Triage must provide or approve that copy; tests should assert the approved contract without coupling to transport internals.

## Testing Decisions

- Tests should verify externally observable behavior through `InviteService`, returned `Invite` values, `RecordingNotifier.sent`, lifecycle results, parsed CSV output, and `display_name` output. They should not assert private helper calls or internal implementation structure.
- Extend the existing `unittest` suite and follow its prior art: inject a fixed clock into `InviteService`, use `RecordingNotifier` instead of a real transport, and test `display_name` directly.
- Test that invite creation stores and returns the invite while recording exactly one SMS to the invite's phone number with the approved body.
- Test explicitly that invite creation records no email notification.
- Test multiple invite creations produce one SMS per invite without duplicates or cross-addressing phone numbers.
- Test that `expires_at` is exactly 30 days after `created_at`.
- Test lifecycle behavior immediately before expiration, exactly at expiration, and after expiration using controlled date-times.
- Test that evaluating expiration does not remove or mutate the stored invite.
- Test finance CSV output for zero, one, and multiple invites, including the exact `name,phone` header and stored row ordering.
- Parse exported CSV with a standards-compliant CSV reader and assert each row has exactly the `name` and `phone` fields.
- Test explicitly that email, creation time, expiration time, status, and arbitrary future invite attributes do not appear as CSV columns or values sourced from those fields.
- Test CSV escaping with commas, quotes, Unicode, and line breaks in supported fields.
- Test that active and expired invites are both included without adding lifecycle columns.
- Test repeated exports return equivalent output for the same collection and do not mutate invites or record notifications.
- Add a regression test proving a wholly Arabic guest name produces a non-blank display name and preserves its text.
- Test Arabic names at, below, and above the length limit to prove truncation is Unicode-safe and deterministic.
- Test mixed Arabic and Latin names, as well as representative non-ASCII names, to guard against another ASCII-only implementation.
- Preserve the existing Latin-name title-casing test and add coverage for leading and trailing whitespace.
- Test that the formatter never returns blank solely because a non-blank input contains Arabic characters.
- Once delivery-failure semantics are resolved in triage, add a service-level test that makes `Notifier.send_sms` raise and verifies the agreed storage and exception behavior.

## Out of Scope

- Invite email notifications of any kind.
- CSV columns other than guest name and phone number.
- Filtering the finance CSV by lifecycle status or selecting a subset of invites.
- CSV import or editing invite data through CSV.
- Notification channels other than SMS.
- Reminder or expiration-notification messages.
- Resending, revoking, deleting, accepting, or redeeming invites.
- Automatically deleting expired invite records.
- Adding database persistence, an HTTP API, authentication, authorization, or a graphical interface.
- Choosing or configuring a production SMS provider.
- Translating or localizing the SMS body.
- Changing pricing behavior.

## Further Notes

- This PRD supersedes both earlier versions. The final requirements are SMS-only notifications, a 30-day invite lifetime, a finance CSV limited to name and phone, and Unicode-safe guest display names.
- The current service stores invites in memory, and this PRD preserves that architecture.
- The 30-day lifetime is a duration from each invite's recorded creation time, not 30 calendar dates.
- The finance CSV's two-column allowlist is intentional. Adding another field requires an explicit future product and privacy decision rather than automatic serialization of the `Invite` model.
- The Arabic-name issue is an existing display defect: byte truncation followed by ASCII decoding drops Arabic characters. Unicode-safe character truncation addresses the cause while retaining the formatter's role.
- This issue carries `needs-triage` because SMS delivery-failure semantics and final SMS copy still require product or engineering confirmation before execution.
